survey: Watch the full video. Mark gameplay, non-game footage and end cards. Choose as few segments as possible, up to 30 seconds each, with cuts near movement starts or camera changes. List scenes, characters, objects and their first clear appearances.
frames: Choose the fewest clear frames covering this segment's scenes, characters, objects and ground, especially newly appearing items. Select existing generated references for content already seen.
image: Convert Image 1 to realistic materials, matching the references' style, color, brightness, shadows and texture.
video: Edit the video: replace its materials to match the reference images.
segment: Compare the result with the source. Report missed realistic materials, content changes, motion changes or artifacts. Ignore issues already present in the source. Apply a relaxed standard to UI, HUD and text: accept mild blur, ghosting or jelly-like deformation while they change or move, provided they look normal when static and their overall placement remains reasonably stable. Do not require pixel-perfect shapes or frame-by-frame text and number matching during changes. Report UI, HUD or text only for obvious drifting, severe distortion, persistent abnormal appearance when static, or major missing or added elements. Do not fail the segment or request a retry for the tolerated UI, HUD or text imperfections. Keep the usual standards for gameplay objects, characters, materials and motion.
tail: Compare Image 1 (the previous generated segment last frame) with Image 2 (the next source segment first frame). Decide only whether these are consecutive views of the same continuous shot. Ignore differences in material realism, texture quality, lighting style and rendering style. Return ok=true for the same continuous shot, otherwise false. List inventory IDs visible in Image 1 without judging materials.
